title: Transformations: Slides, Flips, Turns and Tessellations
seo_title: Grade 5 Transformations Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Draw composite shapes by translating, reflecting and rotating; describe patterns in terms of line symmetry, translation, reflection and rotation; tessellate 2-D shapes.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 5 transformations worksheets: slides, flips, turns, naming transformations and tessellations. 100 questions with memos.
key_big: Slide, flip, turn: the shape stays the same size.
key_sub: A tessellation has no gaps or overlaps.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A translation (slide) moves a shape without turning or flipping it.
  • A reflection (flip) makes a mirror image across a line.
  • A rotation (turn) turns a shape around a point.
  • The shape stays the same size in all three. A tessellation covers a surface with shapes and no gaps or overlaps.

Examples

Example

The shape faces the other way across a line

mirror image

Answer: a reflection

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Flip or turn?A flip makes a mirror image.
Wrong cornerCount from the same corner.
Every shape tessellatesCircles leave gaps.

faq.q: What does CAPS Grade 5 say about transformations?
faq.a: Recognise, describe and perform translations, reflections and rotations with 2-D shapes and 3-D objects, and make tessellations.

faq.q: Does a translation change the size?

faq.a: Squares, rectangles, equilateral triangles and regular hexagons.

items.q: Which sentence is true about a slide (translation)?
c: The shape faces the same way
The shape becomes a mirror image
The shape turns about a point
items.e: A slide moves a shape left or right and up or down. It does not flip or turn, so the shape faces the same way and keeps its size.

items.q: A triangle slides 5 units left. Its top vertex moves 5 units left. How does its bottom-right vertex move?
items.e: In a slide every vertex moves the same distance in the same direction. So every vertex moves 5 units left.

items.q: A square with sides of 4 cm slides 3 units up on grid paper. How long are its sides now?
items.e: A slide only moves the square. It does not stretch it, so the sides are still 4 cm long.

items.q: Point P slides 4 units right. Which point shows where it lands?
items.e: From P, count 4 jumps right. Count the jumps, not the point you start on. P lands on point D. Point A: 1 unit short (the starting point was counted as 1). Point B: it went up, not across. Point C: it went the wrong way.

items.q: Point P slides 3 units down. Which point shows where it lands?
items.e: From P, count 3 jumps down. Count the jumps, not the point you start on. P lands on point C. Point A: 1 unit short (the starting point was counted as 1). Point B: it went the wrong way. Point D: it went right, not down.

items.q: Point P slides 5 units right and 3 units up. Which point shows where it lands?
items.e: From P, count 5 jumps right and 3 jumps up. Count the jumps, not the point you start on. P lands on point B. Point A: 1 unit short (the starting point was counted as 1). Point C: the two moves were mixed up. Point D: only the move right was made.

items.q: Point P slides 5 units left and 4 units up. Which point shows where it lands?
items.e: From P, count 5 jumps left and 4 jumps up. Count the jumps, not the point you start on. P lands on point A. Point B: 1 unit short (the starting point was counted as 1). Point C: only the move left was made. Point D: 1 unit too far.

items.q: Point A slides to point B. Describe the slide.
items.e: A is at (2, 3) and B is at (6, 3). Across: 2 to 6 is 4 units right. The y-coordinate stays 3, so there is no move up or down. Count the jumps, not the point you start on.

items.q: Point A slides to point B. Describe the slide.
items.e: A is at (5, 7) and B is at (5, 2). The x-coordinate stays 5, so there is no move left or right. Up and down: 7 to 2 is 5 units down. Count the jumps, not the point you start on.

items.q: Point A slides to point B. Describe the slide.
items.e: A is at (1, 1) and B is at (6, 4). Across: 1 to 6 is 5 units right. Up and down: 1 to 4 is 3 units up. Count the jumps, not the point you start on.

items.q: Point A is translated to point B. Describe the translation.
items.e: A is at (2, 3) and B is at (5, 1). Across: 2 to 5 is 3 squares right. Up and down: 3 to 1 is 2 squares down. Count the squares you jump, not the lines you touch.

items.q: Point A is translated to point B. Describe the translation.
items.e: A is at (6, 2) and B is at (3, 6). Across: 6 to 3 is 3 squares left. Up and down: 2 to 6 is 4 squares up. Count the squares you jump, not the lines you touch.

items.q: Point A is translated to point B. Describe the translation.
items.e: A is at (1, 1) and B is at (7, 4). Across: 1 to 7 is 6 squares right. Up and down: 1 to 4 is 3 squares up. Count the squares you jump, not the lines you touch.

items.q: Point A is translated to point B. Describe the translation.
items.e: A is at (8, 7) and B is at (4, 2). Across: 8 to 4 is 4 squares left. Up and down: 7 to 2 is 5 squares down. Count the squares you jump, not the lines you touch.

items.q: Point A is translated to point B. Describe the translation.
items.e: A is at (3, 6) and B is at (3, 1). The x-coordinate stays 3, so there is no move left or right. Up and down: 6 to 1 is 5 squares down. Count the squares you jump, not the lines you touch.

items.q: Point A is translated to point B. Describe the translation.
items.e: A is at (2, 5) and B is at (9, 5). Across: 2 to 9 is 7 squares right. The y-coordinate stays 5, so there is no move up or down. Count the squares you jump, not the lines you touch.

items.q: Shape A is translated to shape B. Describe the translation.
items.e: Follow one corner. The corner of A at (1, 5) moves to (6, 1) in B. That is 5 squares right and 4 squares down. Every corner moves the same way.

items.q: Shape A is translated to shape B. Describe the translation.
items.e: Follow one corner. The corner of A at (1, 1) moves to (5, 5) in B. That is 4 squares right and 4 squares up. Every corner moves the same way.

items.q: Shape A is translated to shape B. Describe the translation.
items.e: Follow one corner. The corner of A at (6, 5) moves to (1, 1) in B. That is 5 squares left and 4 squares down. Every corner moves the same way.

items.q: Shape A is translated to shape B. Describe the translation.
items.e: Follow one corner. The corner of A at (1, 4) moves to (5, 1) in B. That is 4 squares right and 3 squares down. Every corner moves the same way.

items.q: What does a flip (reflection) make?
c: a smaller copy of the shape
a mirror image of the shape
the same shape, facing the same way
a bigger copy of the shape
items.e: A flip turns the shape over a line, like a mirror. The image faces the other way, but its size does not change.

items.q: Point P is 3 units to the left of a vertical line of reflection. Where is its image?
c: 2 units to the right of the line
3 units to the left of the line
3 units to the right of the line
6 units to the right of the line
items.e: In a flip the image is the same distance from the line as the point, on the other side. (2 units comes from counting the line as the first jump.)

items.q: Point P is flipped in the dashed line x = 4. Which point is its image?
items.e: P (2, 3) is 2 units to the left of the line x = 4. The image is 2 units to the right of it: 4 + 2 = 6. y stays 3. The image is (6, 3). That is point B. Point A: it is 1 unit too close to the line (the line was counted as the first jump). Point C: it was flipped up or down, not across the line. Point D: x and y are swapped.

items.q: Point P is flipped in the dashed line x = 5. Which point is its image?
items.e: P (8, 6) is 3 units to the right of the line x = 5. The image is 3 units to the left of it: 5 − 3 = 2. y stays 6. The image is (2, 6). That is point A. Point B: it is 1 unit too close to the line (the line was counted as the first jump). Point C: it stops on the line of reflection. Point D: x and y are swapped.

items.q: Point P is flipped in the dashed line y = 3. Which point is its image?
items.e: P (2, 1) is 2 units below the line y = 3. The image is 2 units above it: 3 + 2 = 5. x stays 2. The image is (2, 5). That is point C. Point A: it is 1 unit too close to the line (the line was counted as the first jump). Point B: x and y are swapped. Point D: it was flipped across, not up or down over the line.

items.q: Point P is flipped in the dashed line y = 4. Which point is its image?
items.e: P (5, 6) is 2 units above the line y = 4. The image is 2 units below it: 4 − 2 = 2. x stays 5. The image is (5, 2). That is point D. Point A: it is 1 unit too close to the line (the line was counted as the first jump). Point B: it was flipped across, not up or down over the line. Point C: x and y are swapped.

items.q: The green shape is flipped (reflected) in the dashed line. In which picture is the blue image correct?
items.e: Each vertex of the image must be the same distance from the line as its partner, on the other side. Only C is a true mirror image. Others: A: the shape was turned (it is upside down and back to front), not flipped; B: the shape was slid across, not flipped (it faces the same way); D: the image is 1 unit too close to the line (the line was counted as the first jump).

items.q: The green shape is flipped (reflected) in the dashed line. In which picture is the blue image correct?
items.e: Each vertex of the image must be the same distance from the line as its partner, on the other side. Only D is a true mirror image. Others: A: the shape was flipped the wrong way (left to right), not over the dashed line; B: the shape was turned (it is upside down and back to front), not flipped; C: the image is 1 unit too close to the line (the line was counted as the first jump).

items.q: The green shape is flipped (reflected) in the dashed line. In which picture is the blue image correct?
items.e: Each vertex of the image must be the same distance from the line as its partner, on the other side. Only A is a true mirror image. Others: B: the shape was slid across, not flipped (it faces the same way); C: the image is 1 unit too far from the line; D: the shape was turned (it is upside down and back to front), not flipped.

items.q: Reflect the point (3, 4) in the vertical line x = 5. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: The point (3, 4) is 2 units to the left of the line x = 5. The image is 2 units to the right of it: 5 + 2 = 7. y stays 4. The image is (7, 4).

items.q: Reflect the point (3, 4) in the vertical mirror line x = 5. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: The point (3, 4) is 2 squares to the left of the line x = 5. The image is 2 squares to the right of it: 5 + 2 = 7. y stays 4. The image is (7, 4).

items.q: Reflect the point (8, 2) in the vertical mirror line x = 6. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: The point (8, 2) is 2 squares to the right of the line x = 6. The image is 2 squares to the left of it: 6 − 2 = 4. y stays 2. The image is (4, 2).

items.q: Reflect the point (2, 1) in the horizontal mirror line y = 3. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: The point (2, 1) is 2 squares below the line y = 3. The image is 2 squares above it: 3 + 2 = 5. x stays 2. The image is (2, 5).

items.q: Reflect the point (6, 9) in the horizontal mirror line y = 6. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: The point (6, 9) is 3 squares above the line y = 6. The image is 3 squares below it: 6 − 3 = 3. x stays 6. The image is (6, 3).

items.q: Reflect the point (1, 7) in the vertical mirror line x = 4. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: The point (1, 7) is 3 squares to the left of the line x = 4. The image is 3 squares to the right of it: 4 + 3 = 7. y stays 7. The image is (7, 7).

items.q: Reflect the point (5, 3) in the horizontal mirror line y = 5. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: The point (5, 3) is 2 squares below the line y = 5. The image is 2 squares above it: 5 + 2 = 7. x stays 5. The image is (5, 7).

items.q: Which point is the reflection of point P in the mirror line x = 4?
items.e: P (2, 3) is 2 squares to the left of the line x = 4. The image is 2 squares to the right of it: 4 + 2 = 6. y stays 3. The image is (6, 3). That is point C. Point A: it is 1 square too far (the lines were counted, starting with 1 on the line P is on). Point B: it stops on the mirror line. Point D: it was flipped up or down, not across the line.

items.q: Which point is the reflection of point P in the mirror line x = 5?
items.e: P (7, 5) is 2 squares to the right of the line x = 5. The image is 2 squares to the left of it: 5 − 2 = 3. y stays 5. The image is (3, 5). That is point A. Point B: it is 1 square too far (the lines were counted, starting with 1 on the line P is on). Point C: it stops on the mirror line. Point D: x and y are swapped.

items.q: Which point is the reflection of point P in the mirror line y = 3?
items.e: P (3, 1) is 2 squares below the line y = 3. The image is 2 squares above it: 3 + 2 = 5. x stays 3. The image is (3, 5). That is point D. Point A: it is 1 square too far (the lines were counted, starting with 1 on the line P is on). Point B: it stops on the mirror line. Point C: x and y are swapped.

items.q: Which point is the reflection of point P in the mirror line y = 4?
items.e: P (5, 6) is 2 squares above the line y = 4. The image is 2 squares below it: 4 − 2 = 2. x stays 5. The image is (5, 2). That is point B. Point A: it is 1 square too far (the lines were counted, starting with 1 on the line P is on). Point C: it stops on the mirror line. Point D: it was flipped across, not up or down over the line.

items.q: How many degrees is a quarter turn?
items.e: A full turn is 360°. A quarter turn is one of 4 equal parts: 360° ÷ 4 = 90°. A half turn is 180°.

items.q: Which way do the hands of a clock turn?
items.e: Clock hands go from 12 to 3 to 6 to 9: that is clockwise. The other way is anti-clockwise.

items.q: The minute hand of a clock moves from 12 to 3. What turn is that?
items.e: From 12 to 3 is one quarter of the way around the clock, and clock hands move clockwise.

items.q: A triangle is turned about its vertex A. Which point stays in the same place?
items.e: The centre of rotation (the turn centre) does not move. Here it is vertex A; every other point turns around it.

items.q: A shape makes two quarter turns clockwise about the same point. What is that the same as?
items.e: Each quarter turn is 90°. 90° + 90° = 180°, which is a half turn.

items.q: A shape is turned 180° clockwise about a point. A copy of it is turned 180° anti-clockwise about the same point. Where do they land?
c: one lands twice as far away
one is a mirror image of the other
items.e: A half turn is a half turn, whichever way you go. 180° clockwise and 180° anti-clockwise end in the same place.

items.q: Turn the point B (6, 4) 90° clockwise about the point A (3, 4). Where does B land?
items.e: From A (3, 4), B (6, 4) is 3 right. In a 90° clockwise turn, right turns into down, down into left, left into up and up into right. So from (3, 4), the image is 3 down: (3, 1).

items.q: Turn the point Q (8, 5) 90° anti-clockwise about the point P (5, 5). Where does Q land?
items.e: From P (5, 5), Q (8, 5) is 3 right. In a 90° anti-clockwise turn, right turns into up, up into left, left into down and down into right. So from (5, 5), the image is 3 up: (5, 8).

items.q: A rectangle has vertices K (3, 3), L (5, 3), M (5, 6) and N (3, 6). It is turned 90° clockwise about vertex K. Where does vertex M land?
items.e: From vertex K (3, 3), vertex M (5, 6) is 2 right and 3 up. In a 90° clockwise turn, right turns into down, down into left, left into up and up into right. So from (3, 3), the image is 3 right and 2 down: (6, 1).

items.q: A triangle has vertices A (4, 4), B (1, 5) and C (4, 7). It is turned 180° about vertex A. Where does vertex B land?
items.e: From vertex A (4, 4), vertex B (1, 5) is 3 left and 1 up. In a 180° turn, right turns into left, left into right, up into down and down into up. So from (4, 4), the image is 3 right and 1 down: (7, 3).

items.q: The green shape is turned 90° clockwise about the red dot. In which picture is the blue image correct?
items.e: The red dot does not move. Follow one side: the side from the red dot going right turns to go down in a quarter turn (90°) clockwise. Only B shows that. Others: A: a half turn (180°); C: a quarter turn anti-clockwise; D: a flip (mirror image), not a turn.

items.q: The green shape is turned 90° anti-clockwise about the red dot. In which picture is the blue image correct?
items.e: The red dot does not move. Follow one side: the side from the red dot going right turns to go up in a quarter turn (90°) anti-clockwise. Only D shows that. Others: A: a quarter turn clockwise; B: a flip (mirror image), not a turn; C: a half turn (180°).

items.q: The green shape is turned 180° about the red dot. In which picture is the blue image correct?
items.e: The red dot does not move. Follow one side: the side from the red dot going right turns to go left in a half turn (180°). Only A shows that. Others: B: a quarter turn anti-clockwise; C: a flip (mirror image), not a turn; D: a quarter turn clockwise.

items.q: The green shape is turned 90° clockwise about the red dot. In which picture is the blue image correct?
items.e: The red dot does not move. Follow one side: the side from the red dot going up turns to go right in a quarter turn (90°) clockwise. Only C shows that. Others: A: a half turn (180°); B: a flip (mirror image), not a turn; D: a quarter turn anti-clockwise.

items.q: Point P is turned 90° clockwise about point R. Which point is the image?
items.e: From R (4, 3), P (7, 5) is 3 right and 2 up. In a 90° clockwise turn, right turns into down, down into left, left into up and up into right. So from (4, 3), the image is 2 right and 3 down: (6, 0). That is point A. Point B: turned the wrong way (90° anti-clockwise). Point C: a 180° turn, not 90°. Point D: the numbers were swapped, but the directions were not turned.

items.q: Point P is turned 180° about point R. Which point is the image?
items.e: From R (5, 4), P (3, 7) is 2 left and 3 up. In a 180° turn, right turns into left, left into right, up into down and down into up. So from (5, 4), the image is 2 right and 3 down: (7, 1). That is point C. Point A: a 90° turn clockwise, not 180°. Point B: a 90° turn anti-clockwise, not 180°. Point D: the numbers were swapped, but the directions were not turned.

items.q: A shape is turned about its vertex (4, 4). Another vertex moves from (6, 4) to (4, 2). Describe the turn.
items.e: (6, 4) is 2 right from the centre. (4, 2) is 2 down from the centre. Right turned into down: that is a quarter turn clockwise.

items.q: A shape is turned about its vertex (3, 3). Another vertex moves from (5, 4) to (1, 2). Describe the turn.
items.e: (5, 4) is 2 right and 1 up from the centre. (1, 2) is 2 left and 1 down from the centre. Right turned into left and up turned into down: that is a half turn, 180°.

items.q: Priya turns the point (7, 3) 90° clockwise about (4, 3) and gets (4, 6). What mistake did she make?
items.e: (4, 6) is a quarter turn anti-clockwise. From the centre (4, 3), the point (7, 3) is 3 right. In a 90° clockwise turn, right turns into down, down into left, left into up and up into right. So from (4, 3), the image is 3 down: (4, 0).

items.q: The green shape is turned 90° clockwise about the red dot. In which picture is the blue image correct?
items.e: The red dot does not move. Follow one side: the side from the red dot going right turns to go down in a quarter turn (90°) clockwise. Only C shows that. Others: A: a quarter turn anti-clockwise; B: a flip (mirror image), not a turn; D: a half turn (180°).

items.q: Which transformation is most like SkyTrain moving along a straight piece of track?
items.e: The train moves in a straight line and does not turn or flip, so it is a slide.

items.q: Which transformation is most like the mountains and their upside-down picture in a calm lake?
items.e: The picture in the water is a mirror image, upside down over the shoreline. That is a flip.

items.q: Which transformation is most like a door swinging open on its hinges?
items.e: The door turns about the hinges. The hinges stay still, like a turn centre. That is a turn.

items.q: Which transformation is most like pushing a box straight across the gym floor?
items.e: The box moves across without turning or flipping, so it is a slide.

items.q: Which transformation is most like the hands of a clock moving from 12 to 6?
items.e: The hands turn about the centre of the clock. That is a half turn.

items.q: Which transformation is most like your hand and its image in a mirror?
items.e: A mirror image faces the other way: a right hand looks like a left hand. That is a flip.

items.q: What happened to shape A to make shape B?
items.e: B faces the same way as A and is the same size. Every vertex moved 5 units right and 3 units up, for example (1, 1) → (6, 4). That is a slide.

items.q: What happened to shape A to make shape B?
items.e: In A the long arm of the L lies flat along the bottom. In B it stands straight up. A slide or a flip cannot make a flat arm stand up, but a turn can: B is A turned a quarter turn (90°) clockwise.

items.q: What happened to shape A to make shape B?
items.e: B looks exactly like A and faces the same way. Every vertex moved 5 units right and 4 units down. That is a slide.

items.q: What happened to shape A to make shape B?
items.e: In A the right angle is at the bottom left; in B it is at the top left. B is A flipped over the line y = 4: each vertex is the same distance from the line on the other side. That is a flip.

items.q: What happened to shape A to make shape B?
items.e: B points the same way as A. Every corner moved 5 squares right and 3 squares up, for example (1, 1) → (6, 4). That is a translation.

items.q: What happened to shape A to make shape B?
items.e: B faces the same way as A and is the same size. Every corner moved 5 squares left and 2 squares up. That is a translation.

items.q: What happened to shape A to make shape B?
items.e: The sides of A are 2 squares long. The sides of B are 4 squares long. A translation or a reflection never changes the size.

items.q: What happened to shape A to make shape B?
items.e: A is 4 squares by 2 squares. B is only 2 squares by 1 square, so B is smaller. It is not a translation or a reflection.

items.q: Anika wants to reflect shape A in the dashed mirror line. Is shape B correct?
c: No: it was slid, not flipped
No: it is too far from the line
items.e: Each corner of B is the same distance from the line x = 5 as its partner in A: (1, 2) is 4 squares left of the line and (9, 2) is 4 squares right. B is correct.

items.q: Lethabo wants to reflect shape A in the dashed mirror line. Is shape B correct?
c: No: it was slid, not flipped
No: it is too far from the line
items.e: (1, 1) is 3 squares below the line y = 4, so its image should be 3 squares above, at (1, 7). B is at (1, 8): 1 square too far.

items.q: Kgomotso wants to reflect shape A in the dashed mirror line. Is shape B correct?
c: No: it is too far from the line
No: it was slid, not flipped
items.e: In A the sloping side is on the right. In B it is also on the right, so B points the same way: it was slid. A mirror image would have the sloping side on the left.

items.q: Tshepo wants to reflect shape A in the dashed mirror line. Is shape B correct?
c: No: it is too far from the line
No: it was slid, not flipped
items.e: The sides of A are 2 squares long, but the sides of B are 3 squares long. A reflection never changes the size.

items.q: A triangle with corners at (1, 1), (3, 1), (1, 4) moves to (5, 1), (7, 1), (5, 4). What happened?
items.e: Every corner moved 4 squares right and the y-coordinates stayed the same. The triangle faces the same way: a translation.

items.q: A triangle with corners at (1, 1), (3, 1), (1, 4) moves to (7, 1), (5, 1), (7, 4). What happened?
items.e: (1, 1) moved 6 squares but (3, 1) moved only 2, so it is not a slide. Each corner is the same distance from x = 4 on the other side: a reflection in the line x = 4.

items.q: Shape A was moved to make shape B. What happened to shape A?
items.e: Every corner of B is the same number of squares from its matching corner of A, in the same direction, and B faces the same way. It was slid: a translation. Every corner moved 5 squares right and 4 squares up.

items.q: Shape A was moved to make shape B. What happened to shape A?
items.e: Every corner of B is the same number of squares from its matching corner of A, in the same direction, and B faces the same way. It was slid: a translation. Every corner moved 5 squares right and 4 squares down.

items.q: Shape A was moved to make shape B. What happened to shape A?
items.e: B is a mirror image of A: it faces the other way. Each corner of B is the same distance from the mirror line as its partner in A. It was flipped: a reflection. The mirror line is x = 5.

items.q: Shape A was moved to make shape B. What happened to shape A?
items.e: B is a mirror image of A: it faces the other way. Each corner of B is the same distance from the mirror line as its partner in A. It was flipped: a reflection. The mirror line is y = 4: B is upside down but is not turned.

items.q: Shape A was moved to make shape B. What happened to shape A?
items.e: B is a mirror image of A: it faces the other way. Each corner of B is the same distance from the mirror line as its partner in A. It was flipped: a reflection. The slanted side is on the left of A and on the right of B, at the same height.

items.q: Shape A was moved to make shape B. Point O does not move. What happened to shape A?
items.e: B is A turned about the point O: it is not flipped (it is not a mirror image), and O does not move. It is a rotation. The side that pointed right from O now points down: a quarter turn clockwise.

items.q: Shape A was moved to make shape B. Point O does not move. What happened to shape A?
items.e: B is A turned about the point O: it is not flipped (it is not a mirror image), and O does not move. It is a rotation. It is a half turn about O. It looks upside down, but a reflection in a horizontal line would not also swap left and right.

items.q: Shape A was moved to make shape B. Point O does not move. What happened to shape A?
items.e: B is A turned about the point O: it is not flipped (it is not a mirror image), and O does not move. It is a rotation. The bottom side pointed right from O and now points up: a quarter turn anticlockwise.

items.q: Shape A was moved to make shape B. What happened to shape A?
items.e: The sides of B are twice as long as the sides of A. A translation, reflection or rotation never changes the size, so B was enlarged. The bottom side of A is 3 squares long; the bottom side of B is 6 squares long.

items.q: In which picture is the blue shape a reflection of the green shape?
items.e: In D the blue shape is reflected in a vertical line: it faces the other way, left to right. The others: A is turned a half turn: upside down and back to front; B is turned a quarter turn clockwise; C is slid (a translation): it faces the same way.

items.q: Each angle of a square is 90°. How many squares fit together around one point with no gaps?
items.e: The angles around a point add up to 360°. 360° ÷ 90° = 4, so 4 squares fit exactly around each point.

items.q: Each angle of an equilateral triangle is 60°. How many equilateral triangles fit together around one point with no gaps?
items.e: The angles around a point add up to 360°. 360° ÷ 60° = 6, so 6 equilateral triangles fit exactly around each point.

items.q: Each angle of a regular hexagon is 120°. How many regular hexagons fit together around one point with no gaps?
items.e: The angles around a point add up to 360°. 360° ÷ 120° = 3, so 3 regular hexagons fit exactly around each point.

items.q: Each angle of a regular pentagon is 108°. Can regular pentagons fit around a point with no gaps?
items.e: 3 × 108° = 324°, which is less than 360°, so there is a gap of 36°. 4 × 108° = 432°, which is more than 360°, so a fourth pentagon would overlap. Regular pentagons do not tessellate.

items.q: Three regular pentagons meet at the red dot. Each angle of a regular pentagon is 108°. What is the size of the gap?
items.e: 3 × 108° = 324°. A full turn is 360°, so the gap is 360° − 324° = 36°. No regular shape has a 36° angle, so the gap cannot be filled with the same tiles.

items.q: Each angle of a regular octagon is 135°. Why do regular octagons not tessellate on their own?
items.e: Around a point the angles must add up to exactly 360°. 2 × 135° = 270° leaves a gap and 3 × 135° = 405° is too much. 135° does not divide exactly into 360°.

items.q: What does it mean when a shape tessellates?
c: It has at least one line of symmetry
Copies of it fit together with no gaps and no overlaps
It can be turned onto itself
Copies of it fit together with small gaps between them
items.e: A tessellation is a pattern of shapes that covers a surface with no gaps and no overlaps, like the tiles on a floor.

items.q: Which shape tessellates on its own?
items.e: The regular hexagon (A): each angle is 120° and 3 × 120° = 360°. A regular pentagon (108°) and a regular octagon (135°) leave gaps, and circles cannot fit together without gaps.

items.q: Which shape does NOT tessellate on its own?
items.e: The regular pentagon (B): its angles are 108° and 360° ÷ 108° is not a whole number. Squares (4 × 90°), equilateral triangles (6 × 60°) and regular hexagons (3 × 120°) all fit exactly around a point.

items.q: Why do circles not tessellate?
c: Their curved edges always leave gaps
They have no angles, so they fit anywhere
items.e: When circles touch, there are always curved gaps between them. A tessellation can have no gaps.
